items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had never heard of him, but I did know who Doris Duke was

ctx.x: One night a party came to the Rosatsch and a fellow came up to me and said he was a pianist. He asked me if he could sit down in for a couple of numbers and naturally, I did not refuse him. He was an American, and a fine pianist. He told me his name was Joe, and he was in the party with Doris Duke, the five and ten per cent store heiress. I had never heard of him, but I did know who Doris Duke was, and I later found out that he was not only with her party, but with her... Lucky cat!

The waiter that served the party was a young fellow and when Miss Duke wanted to leave and pay him with a check, he would not accept it. When the waiters in this place served drinks, they had to pay them in advance to the buffet from their pockets and collect from the clients afterwards. The name of Doris Duke funnily didn't mean anything to this young waiter and he insisted that he wanted cash.
